scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): backs the value of study abroad while arguing a universal requirement is unfair; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Living and studying in another country can open a young person's eyes to a whole new way of life.
Some people recommend that colleges should require every student to spend at least one semester studying in a foreign country.
I agree that studying abroad is valuable, but I believe making it compulsory for all students would be unfair and impractical.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why study abroad is valuable

sentences.text: First, studying abroad offers experiences that classrooms at home rarely provide.
Living in a foreign country teaches students about other languages, customs, and ways of thinking.
For example, a student who spends months abroad often returns more independent, open-minded, and mature.
This shows that time in another country can teach lessons no textbook ever could.
Students abroad also build friendships and skills that help them in an increasingly connected world.
Such experiences can shape a person's whole outlook for the rest of her life.
To this extent, studying abroad is clearly a valuable opportunity.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why a universal requirement is unfair

sentences.text: Second, however, forcing every student to study abroad would create serious problems.
Studying in another country is expensive, and many students simply cannot afford the cost.
Consider a student supporting her family who could never pay for a semester overseas.
Such a requirement would unfairly punish poorer students for their circumstances.
Some students also have health needs or family duties that make travelling abroad impossible.
A rule forcing everyone abroad would ignore these very real and personal difficulties.
Studying abroad, then, should be encouraged and supported rather than demanded of all.
In conclusion, spending a semester abroad can be a wonderful and valuable experience.
But requiring it of every student would unfairly burden those who cannot afford or manage it.
The wiser policy is to encourage and fund study abroad while leaving it as a genuine choice.
